title: Weak cosmic censorship, trapped surfaces, and naked singularities for the Einstein vacuum equations

verification.evidence: The weak cosmic censorship conjecture posits that, generically, all singularities in General Relativity arising from regular asymptotically flat initial data should have a complete future null infinity. While this conjecture remains wide open, it has inspired many mathematical works concerning topics such as trapped surface formation and the construction of naked singularities.

notes: Invited review, volume in honour of Yvonne Choquet-Bruhat; open access CC-BY. Used as a map of the field and for journal references; individual theorem claims are still bound to their own primary sources.

title: Naked Singularities for the Einstein Vacuum Equations: The Exterior Solution

verification.evidence: In this work we initiate the mathematical study of naked singularities for the Einstein vacuum equations in 3+1 dimensions by constructing solutions which correspond to the exterior region of a naked singularity. A key element is our introduction of a new type of self-similarity for the Einstein vacuum equations. ... Prior to this work, the only known examples of naked singularities were the solutions constructed by Christodoulou for the spherically symmetric Einstein-scalar-field system, as well as other solutions explored numerically for either the spherically symmetric Einstein equations coupled to suitable matter models or for the Einstein equations in higher dimensions.

notes: Journal reference (Ann. Math. 198(1) 231-391) appears in the bibliography of SRC-001; arXiv abs page itself shows no journal-ref. Metadata-only cross-check pending Annals DOI fetch.

title: Naked Singularities for the Einstein Vacuum Equations: The Interior Solution

verification.evidence: In a previous work [I. Rodnianski and Y. Shlapentokh-Rothman, Naked Singularities for the Einstein Vacuum Equations: The Exterior Solution, arXiv:1912.08478] we constructed solutions to the Einstein vacuum equations in 3+1 dimensions which corresponded to the exterior region of a naked singularity. In this work we construct solutions which correspond to the interior region and show that the two solutions may be glued together to produce a naked singularity.

notes: Preprint only (single v1, 2022); not peer-reviewed as of ledger date. Cited as conditional/unpublished evidence, never as a published theorem.

title: The interior of dynamical vacuum black holes I: The C^0-stability of the Kerr Cauchy horizon

verification.evidence: We prove that for all such data, the maximal Cauchy evolution can be extended across a non-trivial piece of Cauchy horizon as a Lorentzian manifold with continuous metric. ... In particular, if the exterior region of the Kerr family is proven to be dynamically stable---as is widely expected---then it will follow that the C^0-inextendibility formulation of Penrose's celebrated strong cosmic censorship conjecture is in fact false. The proof suggests, however, that the C^0-metric Cauchy horizons thus arising are generically singular in an essential way, representing so-called weak null singularities, and thus that a revised version of strong cosmic censorship holds.

notes: Journal reference and DOI shown on the arXiv abstract page. Antecedent (Kerr exterior stability) must be tracked separately; see SRC on Giorgi-Klainerman-Szeftel.

title: The C^0-inextendibility of the Schwarzschild spacetime and the spacelike diameter in Lorentzian Geometry

verification.evidence: The maximal analytic Schwarzschild spacetime is manifestly inextendible as a Lorentzian manifold with a twice continuously differentiable metric. In this paper, we prove the stronger statement that it is even inextendible as a Lorentzian manifold with a continuous metric. ... The investigation of low-regularity inextendibility criteria is motivated by the strong cosmic censorship conjecture.

notes: Journal ref/DOI from the bibliography of SRC-001; arXiv API record confirms title/authors/abstract.

title: On the proof of the C^0-inextendibility of the Schwarzschild spacetime

verification.evidence: This article presents a streamlined version of the author's original proof of the C^0-inextendibility of the maximal analytic Schwarzschild spacetime. ... we give a more flexible and shorter argument for the inextendibility through the interior region.

title: C^0-inextendibility of the Kasner spacetime

verification.evidence: The Kasner spacetime is a cosmological model of an anisotropic expanding universe without matter and is an exact solution of the Einstein vacuum equations Ric(g) = 0. It is manifestly inextendible as a Lorentzian manifold with a twice differentiable metric. In this thesis we proof that it is even inextendible as a Lorentzian manifold with merely continuous metric.

notes: Thesis, not peer-reviewed. Supporting evidence only.

title: C^0-inextendibility of FLRW spacetimes within a subclass of axisymmetric spacetimes

verification.evidence: Starting from the proof of the C^0-inextendibility of Schwarzschild by Sbierski, the past decade has seen renewed interest in showing low-regularity inextendibility for known spacetime models. ... we present an extension of work by Galloway and Ling on C^0-inextendibility of certain FLRW spacetimes within a subclass of spherically symmetric spacetimes, to C^0-inextendibility within a subclass of axisymmetric spacetimes.

notes: Preprint; supporting evidence for cosmology-side C^0 methods.

title: C^0-inextendibility of a class of warped-product black hole spacetimes

verification.evidence: We adapt Sbierski's proof of C^0-inextendibility of the maximal analytic Schwarzschild spacetime to a broad class of warped-product black hole spacetimes with a static exterior region. ... Under suitable assumptions, including that the fibre is closed (compact without boundary), connected, homogeneous, and orientable, we establish future C^0-inextendibility for spacetimes in this class.

notes: Recent (Jun 2026) preprint; captured to prevent a stale ledger.
